final_report.summary: Across 2 cycles, this mission successfully applied and validated 5 targeted bug fixes to the AtlasForge dashboard's Activity log subsystem. Cycle 1 identified and applied all 5 fixes to dashboard_v2.py, af_engine.py, dashboard_static/js/chat.js, and dashboard_static/src/chat.js. Cycle 2 performed functional validation of every fix, confirmed end-to-end suggestion message flow from af_engine.py through the WebSocket to the Activity log UI, verified distinct styling for system/suggestion messages, confirmed no regressions for normal user/assistant messages, and produced a validated artifact document.
key_achievements: Fixed watch_chat() pre-seeding order: messages now emitted to existing clients BEFORE adding to seen_messages set, eliminating race condition where new connections missed in-flight messages
Expanded watch_chat() poll window from history[-10:] to history[-30:] to match the REST API window, ensuring Activity log and REST endpoint show consistent history depth
_normalize_provider() now preserves 'system' and 'suggestion' as valid provider types instead of remapping them, enabling distinct styling in the Activity log
socket.on('message') in chat.js correctly passes provider/display_role as the 4th argument to addMessage(), fixing missing provider badges in the UI
af_engine.py suggestion events confirmed to use 'system' or 'suggestion' as the provider value, completing the end-to-end suggestion display pipeline
All 5 fixes validated end-to-end with functional testing; no regressions in normal message display
challenges_overcome: Race condition in pre-seeding logic required careful ordering of emit vs. set-insertion operations
Provider normalization had to balance canonicalizing known providers (anthropic, openai, google) while preserving passthrough for special types (system, suggestion)
JavaScript socket event handler required matching the exact argument signature of addMessage() to pass provider correctly
Validating end-to-end suggestion flow required confirming the chain: af_engine emit → WebSocket → chat.js handler → addMessage() → Activity log render
lessons_learned: When fixing message pipeline bugs, always trace the full data path from source (af_engine) through transport (WebSocket) to render (JS/CSS) — partial fixes cause subtle display failures
History window mismatches between REST and WebSocket endpoints create confusing inconsistencies; always keep them in sync
Provider normalization functions should explicitly whitelist passthrough values (system, suggestion) rather than silently remapping unknowns to 'unknown'
Pre-seeding logic for new connections must emit THEN record, never record THEN emit — the reverse order creates a window where messages are lost
Cycle 2 validation loops are valuable: forcing explicit re-confirmation of each fix catches cases where a fix was applied incorrectly or partially reverted
